title: College Football model recap — 2026-09-11
summary: The model went 16/19 (84%) on graded College Football picks.
body: Matchday's model graded 19 College Football picks this stretch, hitting on 16 of them (84%). Over the same 18 games with a market line, the betting market favorite hit 89% of the time.

On calibration: picks stated at 70-80% hit 100% of the time (5 games); picks stated at 80-90% hit 80% of the time (5 games); picks stated at 90+% hit 100% of the time (6 games). A well-calibrated model's stated confidence should roughly match its actual hit rate in each band.
The strongest signal lately has been talent or squad quality: when it favored a side, that side won 89% of the time (18 games).

This is Matchday's own model reporting on itself for anyone to use. Every pick is locked before kickoff and graded automatically once the game finishes; none are rewritten after the fact. See the Q&A page for how the model works.

title: College Football model recap — 2026-09-04
summary: The model went 9/11 (82%) on graded College Football picks.
body: Matchday's model graded 11 College Football picks this stretch, hitting on 9 of them (82%). Over the same 10 games with a market line, the betting market favorite hit 90% of the time.

On calibration: picks stated at 70-80% hit 100% of the time (3 games); picks stated at 80-90% hit 67% of the time (3 games); picks stated at 90+% hit 100% of the time (4 games). A well-calibrated model's stated confidence should roughly match its actual hit rate in each band.
The strongest signal lately has been talent or squad quality: when it favored a side, that side won 90% of the time (10 games).

Among this week's College Football storylines: the biggest upset was Colorado winning 13-14 against Georgia Tech (the market gave that result only about 32%); the model's best call was Utah in Utah vs Idaho at 92% confidence; its biggest miss was picking Rutgers in Rutgers vs Massachusetts, but Massachusetts won instead.
